sessions.title: Inputs and returned answers
sessions.text: An input is a value a method receives. The return type tells us what kind of answer it gives back. boolean means true or false. % gives the remainder after division.
sessions.example:
boolean isPositive(int n) { return n > 0; }
For n = 7: 7 > 0 is true, so the method returns true. System.out.println(isPositive(7)); displays true.
sessions.tiny: For an even-number method, should input 7 return true or false?
sessions.feedback: false: 7 divided by 2 leaves remainder 1.
sessions.reflection: What was the main idea today?

sessions.title: A loop repeats work
sessions.text: A for loop has a starting value, a condition, and an update. i++ changes i by one. i + 1 on its own only calculates a value.
sessions.example:
for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { System.out.println(i); }
// prints 1, then 2, then 3; stops when i is 4.
sessions.tiny: What prints if the condition is i < 3 instead?
sessions.feedback: 1 and 2. At 3 the condition is false.
sessions.reflection: What mistake would you now notice sooner?
sessions.recall: If x starts at 3, what is x after x = x + 2?
